newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed, local bonds retain rise.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed, local bonds retain rise.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mixed Thursday as Brady bonds slipped with U.S. Treasuries and local bonds retained early gains.
"I remain positive for the markets, there are good expectations," said Hugo Diaz Lourenco, chief analyst at private consultancy C&E Consultores.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.35 to 120.65, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 1/8 to 84-6/8.
Lourenco said the market continues "to enjoy good international market conditions," most notably in the form of the low yield on long U.S. Treasury bonds.

But there was slim activity again this session, a situation one trader said could continue until the end of the year because many investors have already clocked up large gains in 1996 giving them little inspiration to re-enter the market before 1997.
In the money markets, call money rates were stable at 6.15 percent.
